messages:
IncidentBot: PAGE: P1 possible cross-tenant KV-cache exposure detected in dedicated-pool-3 (enterprise VPC: acme-vpc). Pager routed to oncall-alex. Brief: some requests with tenant-id headers for tenant-642 observed served by nodes pinned to tenant-701's capacity. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/kv-isolation

Alex (oncall): Acked. Oncall here — starting triage. What evidence do we have (logs/sample keys)?

Jordan SRE: Seeing noisy delta in routing table + access logs. Sample log (scrubbed):

```
2026-03-15T12:31:10Z node-37 dedicated-pool-3 req_id=abcd1234 tenant_id=701 proxied_tenant=642 op=kv_get key=acme-user-642:session:xyz
2026-03-15T12:31:12Z node-38 dedicated-pool-3 req_id=abcd1235 tenant_id=701 proxied_tenant=642 op=kv_get key=acme-user-642:cache:profile
```

Jordan SRE: Those proxied_tenant fields are from our routing metadata — suggests requests originating on 701 nodes are resolving cache keys that map to 642 namespaced keys. Could be a cache normalization bug or misrouted backend call.

Leah - Eng ML: Quick hypothesis: a recent change in prefix normalization (we rolled a small opt in for faster key truncation) combined with a custom tenant prefix for AcmeCorp produced overlapping normalized keys. In short: cache key collision across tenants when prefix "acme-" used + kv-sharding heuristic.

Maya (Security): Recommendation: immediate isolation of dedicated-pool-3 from production traffic, rotate tokens/keys for potentially impacted tenants (AcmeCorp and tenant-642), and snapshot forensic data. Also start a full audit of access logs and possible exports.

Oliver (CS): I'm contacting AcmeCorp product/security lead now. Sending holding message: "We detected an anomalous routing pattern affecting VPC-dedicated pool assigned to your tenant. We're investigating and will update in 30 minutes."

Ryan Ops: I'll remove the pool from LB and drain connections. Planned steps:
- kubectl cordon/drain nodes in dedicated-pool-3
- update envoy upstream to stop routing to pool ID dedicated-pool-3
- snapshot disk + collect /var/log/redwood/kv-*.log

Ryan Ops: Executing: `kubectl label node node-37 no-route=true && kubectl drain node-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Alex (oncall): Done — drain started. New incoming requests should not hit nodes in dedicated-pool-3. Can someone confirm ALB health and that new requests route to fallback pool?

Jordan SRE: Confirmed. ALB removed backend set for pool 3 at 12:36Z. We see 0 new connections to that pool. Continuing audit on historical logs.

Jordan SRE: Running audit script: `/opt/tools/kv-routing-audit.sh --pool dedicated-pool-3 --since 2026-03-15T12:00Z` Output snippet: 

```
[12:34:58] FOUND cross-tenant-hit req_id=abcd1209 origin_tenant=701 target_key_namespace=acme-user-642 count=2
[12:35:09] FOUND cross-tenant-hit req_id=abcd1234 origin_tenant=701 target_key_namespace=acme-user-642 count=1
Total cross-tenant hits: 3
Potentially impacted keys (scrubbed): acme-user-642:session:*, acme-user-642:cache:profile:*
```

Leah - Eng ML: We can push a config fix to enforce tenant-scoped cache prefixes in envoy/filter layer immediately — small change: set tenant-scoped key header and drop requests that don't match. Sample patch: 

```
filters:
  - name: tenant_key_enforcer
    config:
      require_header: x-tenant-id
      prefix_mode: enforce-scoped
```

Leah - Eng ML: I'll open a PR and push to canary (non-customer-facing) once ops confirms traffic is stopped.

Maya (Security): Initiating token rotation for affected tenant scopes. AcmeCorp tokens rotated at 12:40Z (rot_id=rot-9832). Requesting KMS team to check whether any long-lived keys were exported. Also starting forensic snapshot job: `forensic-snapshot --pool dedicated-pool-3 --dest s3://forensic/1839991234/`

Oliver (CS): AcmeCorp replied: they observed two anomalous requests in logs correlated with our timestamps, but they haven't confirmed data exfil. They've asked for a timeline and what keys were accessed. Preparing a data access summary.

Jordan SRE: I've exported matching request traces and uploaded to secure bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1839991234/traces.tar.gz` — contains scrubbing markers. Also attaching a minimal set of indicators for CS: request IDs and timestamps.

Alex (oncall): Action list so far:
- Ops (Ryan): isolate pool + snapshots (in progress)
- SRE (Jordan): run audit + collect traces (done: uploaded)
- Eng-ML (Leah): patch to enforce tenant-key scoping (PR open)
- Security (Maya): rotate tokens + forensic snapshot (started)
- CS (Oliver): customer comms + data access summary (in progress)

Ryan Ops: Snapshot completed: snapshot-id snap-20260315-183999. Disk images copied to s3 (encrypted). Nodes are cordoned and will remain offline until we have a clear remediation.

Leah - Eng ML: Pushed tenant_key_enforcer to canary (routing canary). Observed zero cross-tenant hits for canary traffic. Opening rollback-safe rollout to remaining nodes when cleared. PR: https://redwood/pull/5277

Maya (Security): Forensics complete for initial window. No evidence of bulk export; we saw read operations for a handful of keys (as audit shows). Marking incident potential exposure; severity P1 -> still P1 until final confirmation. We've started an internal case: SEC-2026-091.

Oliver (CS): Sent interim notification to AcmeCorp: "We've taken your pool offline, rotated relevant tokens, and are conducting a forensic review. We'll provide full timeline and indicators by 14:30Z." They're requesting log extracts for 12:30–12:40Z. Jordan, can you provide those extracts as a csv?

Jordan SRE: Uploaded csv to secure share: `https://secure.redwood/share/1839991234/acme-extract.csv` (access restricted).

Alex (oncall): Next steps: keep pool isolated, coordinate with Eng-ML to deploy patch, once patch validated we can plan a controlled restore with monitoring and abort on any mismatch. Also create a formal incident ticket.

Alex (oncall): Created incident ticket INC-4321 and assigned to eng/ops/sre (link: https://jira.redwood/INC-4321).

Ryan Ops: Before we restore, ops will run a safety sweep: re-run audit script, confirm zero cross-tenant hits for 1h of canary traffic, and ensure no stale routes in lb config.

Maya (Security): Please hold on any full restore until we confirm token rotations and KMS audit. I'll post confirmation once rotation and KMS checks are done.

Oliver (CS): AcmeCorp acknowledged the interim note and asked for a postmortem and timeline. We'll coordinate the customer-facing summary once SEC gives green light.

Alex (oncall): Handoff note — my oncall ends in ~45 minutes. Priya is next oncall. Short summary for handoff: P1 possible cross-tenant KV cache exposure in dedicated-pool-3 impacting AcmeCorp (tenant-642). Pool isolated and drained, tokens rotated, forensics snapshot uploaded, patch (tenant_key_enforcer) pushed to canary and showing no regressions. Jira INC-4321 created. Open owners: validate KMS audit (Maya), finish canary monitoring (Leah/Jordan), customer comms and timeline (Oliver).

Priya (oncall-next): Acknowledged — taking over at handoff. I'll coordinate the restore window if SEC signs off. Please add any outstanding asks to INC-4321.

Alex (oncall): Thanks team. I'll remain available until handoff.

(Reaction summary: :rotating_light: x5, :white_check_mark: x3)
